tooltip.name: The name of the element.
tooltip.symbol: A one- or two-letter symbol representing an element.
tooltip.atomic: The number of protons in an atom. This number is unique to each element.
tooltip.mass: A value representing the average mass of an atom.
tooltip.category: A classification that groups elements with similar properties.
tooltip.block: A classification based on the type of orbital occupied by the last electron in the electron configuration. There are s-, p-, d-, and f-blocks.
tooltip.state: The physical state of the element under normal conditions: solid, liquid, or gas.
tooltip.energyLevels: The number of electrons in each electron shell. For example, "2, 8, 1" means there are 2 electrons in the first shell, 8 in the second, and 1 in the third.
tooltip.configuration: Shows how many electrons occupy each orbital. For example, "1s1" means that one electron occupies the 1s orbital.
tooltip.ionization: The energy required to remove one electron from an atom.
tooltip.spectralAnalysis: The light emitted by an element separated by wavelength. Each element has a characteristic pattern.
tooltip.bohrModel: A model that represents how electrons are arranged around the nucleus.
tooltip.bohrModel2: This is the Bohr model. It represents how electrons are arranged around the nucleus.
tooltip.group: A vertical column in the periodic table. Elements in the same group may have similar properties.
tooltip.period: A horizontal row in the periodic table. Elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells.
tooltip.meltingPoint: The temperature at which a solid begins to change into a liquid.
tooltip.boilingPoint: The temperature at which a liquid boils and changes into a gas.
tooltip.heat: The amount of energy required to raise the temperature of a substance by 1 K.
tooltip.thermalConductivity: A value describing how easily heat passes through a substance.
tooltip.radius: A radius used as a measure of the approximate size of an atom.
tooltip.density: The amount of mass contained in a given volume.
tooltip.atomicVolume: The approximate volume occupied by 1 mol of an element.
tooltip.valence: An approximate measure of the number of bonds an atom can form with other atoms.
tooltip.oxidationStates: The charge value considered to be associated with an element in a compound or ion.
tooltip.electronegativity: A measure of how strongly an atom attracts electrons in a chemical bond.
tooltip.electronAffinity: The energy released or absorbed when an atom gains one electron.
tooltip.radioactive: The property of an atomic nucleus of changing spontaneously and emitting radiation in the process.
tooltip.discoveryDate: The year in which the element was discovered.
tooltip.abundance: How much of the element is present.
tooltip.linear: A method that displays values according to their actual rate of increase.
tooltip.logarithmic: A method that represents values using a logarithmic scale, making very large and small values easier to compare.

visualizeOption.description.category: Elements are classified according to their properties. By comparing elements in the same category, you can see the characteristics of each group.
visualizeOption.description.blocks: Elements are divided into s, p, d, and f blocks according to their electron configurations. You can see the relationship between an element's position in the periodic table and its electron configuration.
visualizeOption.description.state: Shows whether an element is a solid, liquid, or gas at the specified temperature and at 1 atm (the atmospheric pressure on Earth).
visualizeOption.description.atomicMass: Atomic mass is the value that represents the mass of one atom. You can see how the mass of atoms differs between elements.
visualizeOption.description.energyLevels: Electron shells are regions around the nucleus where electrons are found. This display uses the number of electrons in the outermost shell of each period to show elements with different colours.
visualizeOption.description.configuration: Electron configuration describes how electrons are arranged in an atom. This display focuses on the last part of the electron configuration to show elements with different colours.
visualizeOption.description.meltPoint: The melting point is the temperature at which a solid begins to become a liquid. You can compare how the melting point differs between elements.
visualizeOption.description.boilPoint: The boiling point is the temperature at which a liquid begins to become a gas. You can compare how the boiling point differs between elements.
visualizeOption.description.density: Density is the amount of mass contained in a given volume. You can see how much the density differs between elements.
visualizeOption.description.electronegativity: Electronegativity describes how strongly an atom attracts electrons when forming a chemical bond. You can see how the ability to attract electrons differs between elements.
visualizeOption.description.electronAffinity: Electron affinity describes the change in energy when an atom receives one electron. You can see how the tendency to receive electrons differs between elements.
visualizeOption.description.ionization: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove one electron from an atom. You can compare how easily electrons can be removed from different elements.
visualizeOption.description.valence: Valence is an indication of the number of bonds an atom can form when bonding with other atoms. It provides a clue to how an element can bond with other elements.
visualizeOption.description.heat: Specific heat is the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of a substance by 1 K. You can see how easily different elements heat up.
visualizeOption.description.thermalConductivity: Thermal conductivity describes how easily heat can travel through a material. You can compare how easily different elements conduct heat.
visualizeOption.description.oxidationStates: Oxidation state is a number that represents the state of an atom in a compound or ion. You can see what states an element can have in chemical reactions.
visualizeOption.description.radius: Atomic radius is an indication of the size of an atom. You can see how the size of atoms changes between elements.
visualizeOption.description.atomicVolume: Atomic volume represents the volume occupied by 1 mol of an element. You can compare how the volume occupied by atoms differs between elements.
visualizeOption.description.spectralAnalysis: An emission spectrum is a characteristic pattern of light seen when an element emits light. Because it differs between elements, it can be used as a clue to identify an element.
visualizeOption.description.bohrModel: The Bohr model represents how electrons are arranged around the nucleus. You can see how the arrangement of electrons differs between elements.
visualizeOption.description.radioactiveEl: Radioactive elements are elements whose nuclei change and release radiation. This display shows which elements are radioactive.
visualizeOption.description.discoveryDate: Shows the year when the element was first discovered. You can compare when different elements were discovered.
visualizeOption.description.abundance: Shows how much of an element exists in different places in nature. You can see how the abundance of elements differs depending on the location.
visualizeOption.description.abundance-universe: Shows the amount of each element present in the universe. You can compare which elements are more or less abundant in the universe.
visualizeOption.description.abundance-solar: Shows the amount of each element present in the Sun. You can see which elements are more abundant in the Sun.
visualizeOption.description.abundance-meteor: Shows the amount of each element contained in meteorites. You can compare how much of each element is present in meteorites.
visualizeOption.description.abundance-crust: Shows the amount of each element present in Earth's crust. You can see which elements are more abundant in the crust.
visualizeOption.description.abundance-ocean: Shows the amount of each element present in the oceans. You can see which elements are more abundant in the oceans.
visualizeOption.description.abundance-human: Shows the amount of each element present in the human body. You can see which elements are more abundant in the human body.
